title: Brief a Plate Like a Pro
hook: Ten miles out is a terrible place to meet your approach plate.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds, kid. Briefing an approach plate. Top to bottom, same order every time — like reading a menu, except the special is granite.
Start at the top briefing strip: frequencies, final approach course, runway. Then the notes — that's where the plate hides the fine print.
Then the plan view for the big picture, and the profile view for the step-downs: final approach fix, glidepath, and where the missed begins.
Finish with minimums and the missed approach — out loud. If you can't say the missed from memory at the fix, kid, you briefed a bedtime story, not an approach.
Strip, notes, plan, profile, minimums, missed. Brief it before the approach environment briefs you.
Instrument Procedures Handbook, chapter four. The FAA wrote four hundred pages so you'd read six.

quiz.question: A solid approach brief flows in what order?
choices: Briefing strip, notes, plan view, profile, minimums, missed
Missed approach, then plan view, then strip
Whatever order the plate prints them
quiz.explanation: Top-to-bottom keeps the brief consistent and complete — ending with minimums and the missed so they're freshest.

quiz.question: Why brief the missed approach out loud before the FAF?
choices: At minimums there's no time to read — you fly it from memory
ATC requires a readback of the missed
It's only needed for circling approaches
So your passenger can fly it
quiz.explanation: The missed happens at the busiest, lowest moment of the approach. The first steps must already be loaded in your head.
